subject: Hospitality
title: Cocktail Cost and Creativity
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Cocktail Cost and Creativity.

hook.text: A craft cocktail sold for $16 often costs under $3 to make. That 80%+ margin makes the bar the highest-return hospitality area.

buildup.text: Cocktail costs come from spirits, mixers, garnishes, and ice. Premium spirits raise costs but also justify higher prices.

discovery.text: Signature cocktails—unique to the venue—command higher prices because they can't be comparison-shopped elsewhere.

twist.text: The garnish often costs more than the liquid. An edible flower or dehydrated citrus wheel can add $1–2 per drink.

climax.text: Bar menus now tell stories: ingredient origins, inspiration, and suggested pairings.

punchline.text: $3 to make, $16 to buy. Cocktails are hospitality's highest-margin art form.

quiz.question: Why are signature cocktails especially profitable?
options: They can't be comparison-shopped elsewhere—exclusivity justifies higher prices
